passage: Dhruv, sixteen, was on the crowded local bus to the town school when it hit. His heart hammered, the world tilted and a voice in his head screamed that something terrible was happening. He pushed off at the next stop and sat under a neem tree, sweating, sure he was dying. After some minutes it faded. passage:

Right after the chemistry exam, Vandana suddenly grabbed the corridor railing. She was breathing fast and said, "My heart, I can't, something's wrong." People started crowding round. I asked them to give us space, and they moved back.
I stayed next to her but didn't hold her. I talked slowly. "I'm here. You're safe. This will pass." I didn't argue when she said she was dying; I just kept saying it will pass and counted slow breaths out loud. After a few minutes her shoulders dropped.
Later, over samosas, she said this was the third time this month. I told her that's worth a proper check, and asked if she'd tell her mum and see the school counsellor. She said she would, tomorrow.
Eshaan

passage: "Minakshi, you're avoiding the train to college since that bad day? I understand. When I was twenty, in Mumbai, I had my first panic on a packed local train at Dadar.
